---
title: "Configuration"
guide-section: "Reference"
---

What a dataset is made of on disk, what `tether.toml` can say, where
credentials and other per-checkout settings live, and what a cloned dataset
can and cannot make tether do.

## Layout

```
<dataset-root>/
  tether.toml                 # committed: format version, dataset id, snapshot/verify/new settings,
                              #   default policies, non-secret backend options
  .tether/
    .gitignore                # ignores workspace.toml, ops.jsonl, secrets.toml, cache/, lock
    secrets.toml              # per checkout: credentials or references, endpoints, executables, SQL
    objects/<key>.toml        # committed, one per object: kind, locator, policy, state, pin,
                              #   recoverable, captured_at, origin (only when "created")
    listings/<hash>.jsonl     # committed, content-addressed per-file listings of directory and
                              #   prefix states (for `diff --content`); pruned by gc
    workspace.toml            # per checkout: workspace id, bookmark, working refs, pending forks,
                              #   base states, fork points, last snapshot
    ops.jsonl                 # per checkout: the operation log

<vcs shared dir>/           # .jj/repo/ or .git/: one per clone, shared by its checkouts, never committed
  tether.lock                 # the repository-wide lock (see Caveats)
  tether-pinned.jsonl         # pins this clone created: the only ones gc releases by default
  tether-created.jsonl        # stores this clone made with `add --create`
  tether-touched.jsonl        # stores this clone forked a branch in or pinned
```

The three per-checkout files are refused while the VCS tracks them (the
[security model](#security-model)). The indexes live with the repository,
not in history or a checkout: an abandoned fork takes the manifest that
named a store with it, and `forget-workspace` takes the checkout's files.
They are memories, not authority. [Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd)
says how `gc` uses them, and why a re-clone starts without them.

`pin_id = <dataset-id>.<blake2b(kind, locator identity, content state)[:16]>`,
and the native ref is `tether.<pin_id>`. An identical state yields the same
pin within a dataset: re-committing an unchanged object is a no-op, and
identical states dedupe to one pin. The identity is the backend's canonical
form of the locator, such as a resolved local path
([Backends](09-backends.qmd#conventions)).

## `tether.toml`

A dataset's configuration is `tether.toml` at the dataset root, committed
with the manifests and loaded into `RepoConfig`. Every key but
`[dataset] id` has a default. A dataset whose version is older than this
tether's is refused by every command except
[`tether upgrade`](07-cli.qmd#upgrade).

```toml
[tether]
version = 5         # the format this tether writes; older datasets need `tether upgrade`

[dataset]
id = "0a1b2c3d"      # 8 hex chars; the namespace of this dataset's pins and branches in every store

[snapshot]
auto = false         # `status` shows the last snapshot (--snapshot refreshes); true: fingerprint on every status

[verify]
on_status = false    # also run a cheap verify of each committed object in status

[new]
fork = "lazy"        # "lazy": create a working branch on first writable open; "eager": during `new`

[defaults]           # policy for objects added without an explicit one
file = "immutable"   # immutable | versioned
pin = "native"       # native | record

[vcs]
prefer = "jj"        # which adapter to use when both .jj and .git exist
trunk = "main"       # the bookmark that stands for every object's upstream branch

[backends.file]      # non-secret options only; one table per kind
storage_options = { region = "us-west-2" }
```

## Dataset id

`init` generates `[dataset] id`, and every clone shares it. Every native ref
carries it (pins `tether.<id>.<hash>`, working branches
`tether.ws.<id>.<bookmark>`), and `gc` stays inside that namespace. So
datasets can share one Icechunk repository or Neon project without deleting
each other's pins. Datasets from before the id existed get one from
`tether upgrade`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not change the id after committing

- Pins and branches made under the old id stop being this dataset's: `gc`
  treats them as foreign and leaves them alone.
- `repair` recreates the pins the manifests name, under the new id.
- A fork meant to become an *independent* dataset must change the id
  *before* it pins anything, or the two share a namespace and can `gc` each
  other.
:::

## Policies

A `Policy` is stored per object (`[policy]` in its manifest). It is set with
the `--file` and `--pin` options of `tether add` (or `Repo.add(policy=...)`)
and changed with `tether set KEY... --file|--pin`. Whether writes fork or
land upstream is not a policy: the trunk writes upstream, and any other
bookmark forks. Manifests from before 0.1.0a9 carry a `write` key, which is
ignored and dropped by `tether upgrade`.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `immutable` (default), `versioned` | `file` backend only. `immutable`: any drift is an error at `status`. `versioned`: a single object in a versioning-enabled bucket or container is Addressable through its version id. |
| `pin` | `native` (default), `record` | Any backend. `record` drops `PIN`: `commit` records the state without a native ref, and `new` forks from the recorded state. Cheaper, but recoverable only while the system keeps that state ([Lever 1](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#lever-1-do-not-pin-what-you-will-not-need---pin-record)). |

## Backend options

`[backends.<kind>]` is handed to the backend when it is first used. The
committed file may set only what a backend allowlists: `storage_options`
for `file`, `delta` and `lance`, and `catalog` for `iceberg`. Inside those
tables only the named keys pass (`region`, `allow_http`,
`virtual_hosted_style_request`, `conditional_put`; `type`, `warehouse`,
`name`). Any other key is refused by name, so an option tether has never
heard of cannot reach a store from a clone. Everything else goes in
`.tether/secrets.toml`, where the same tables may hold any key. Per-backend
keys: [Backends](09-backends.qmd).

## Trust boundary: `.tether/secrets.toml` {#trust-boundary-tethersecretstoml}

A cloned dataset is untrusted input. `tether.toml` and the manifests arrive
with every clone, so nothing in them may choose an executable, an endpoint
your credentials go to, SQL to run, or the variable a secret is read from.
tether refuses a committed `tether.toml` that tries (`[vcs] git_path`,
`[import] query`, `[backends.neon] api_url`, `[backends.ducklake]
init_sql`, a `storage_options.endpoint`, ...), and says where the key
belongs: `.tether/secrets.toml`, per checkout and never committed, or the
environment.

```toml
[vcs]
git_path = "/usr/bin/git"                 # or TETHER_GIT / TETHER_JJ in the environment
# jj_path = "/opt/jj/bin/jj"

[backends.neon]                           # per-kind options the committed file may not set
api_key_env = "NEON_API_KEY"

[backends.ducklake]
init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET (TYPE S3, PROVIDER credential_chain)"]

[uris."s3://lab-a-bucket/"]               # every object whose store URI starts here
profile = "lab-a"                          # an AWS shared-config profile ...
# role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/lab-a"   # ... or a role, assumed via STS ...
# access_key_id = "..."                    # ... or, when nothing else will do, literal keys
# secret_access_key = "..."
# endpoint_url = "http://seaweedfs.local:8333"
# allow_http = true                        # icechunk: plain HTTP to that endpoint
# force_path_style = true                  # icechunk: bucket in the path, not the host

[objects."zarr/imaging"]                  # one object; beats a URI prefix
profile = "imaging"

[uris."mysql://dolt.internal:3306"]       # a Dolt server: the only one sent this password
user = "svc"                              #   (Dolt reads server entries only)
password_env = "DOLT_PASSWORD"

[import]                                  # the default SQL for `tether import` (see Registries and SQL)
query = "SELECT name AS key, 'file' AS kind, uri FROM catalog"
```

Resolution per object, first match wins: `[objects."<key>"]`, then the
longest matching `[uris."<prefix>"]`, then `[backends.<kind>]`, then the
environment and instance credential chain. Per-object entries also reach
`add --create` and `gc --delete-stores`. `file`, `delta` and `lance` take
the entries as storage options, and `icechunk` passes them to `s3_storage`.
Dolt honours only the server's `[uris."mysql://host:port"]` entry (or one
for `mysql://host:port/database`), because the manifest chooses the host a
password is sent to.

A `profile` or `role_arn` is resolved through `boto3` (install it when you
use them) into explicit credentials. Concurrent callers share one
resolution, cached until five minutes before the keys expire. Icechunk
takes a profile or role as a refreshing credential source, so a session
held for hours gets fresh keys instead of failing mid-write.

The file may hold literal credentials, so tether warns when other users can
read it (`chmod 600`) and never prints its contents: not in `status`, not in
`--json`, not in an error. `init` lists it in `.tether/.gitignore`, and
`Repo.find` adds the entry to an older dataset that lacks it.

### Advanced: two stores, two identities

The case the per-URI and per-object entries exist for: a dataset tracks an
Icechunk repository in the imaging lab's account and another in the
sequencing core's, and one `commit` pins both. With `from_env` alone that
is an `AWS_PROFILE` switch between commands, which one `commit` cannot do.

```bash
tether add zarr/imaging s3://imaging-lab-data/plate-01.icechunk --kind icechunk
tether add zarr/reads   s3://seqcore-archive/run-2026-09.icechunk --kind icechunk
```

```toml
# .tether/secrets.toml (this checkout only; never committed)
[uris."s3://imaging-lab-data/"]      # every object in the imaging bucket
profile = "imaging-lab"              # a profile in ~/.aws/config

[objects."zarr/reads"]               # one object, whichever bucket it is in
role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/seqcore-reader"
region = "us-east-2"
```

`tether commit` now opens `zarr/imaging` with the `imaging-lab` profile's
keys and `zarr/reads` with a session assumed into the sequencing core's
role, in one process. A third object with no entry keeps the ambient
environment, and the manifests record only the two URIs.

On CI the same layout works with literal keys the runner writes into the
file before the first command. tether does not expand `${...}` itself, so
write the values in, or use a role the runner's identity can assume
([A CI recipe](13-sharing-and-ci.qmd#a-ci-recipe)).

## Security model

What a cloned dataset (its `tether.toml`, manifests, history, and every
other file in the checkout) can and cannot make tether do.

It cannot:

- **Run a program.** Executables come from `secrets.toml` or the
  environment. `secrets.toml`, `workspace.toml` and `ops.jsonl` are refused
  while the VCS tracks them, since a clone brings a tracked copy with it.
  `find` checks, and so does every later refresh (each `open`, each writing
  command) that finds `workspace.toml` changed.
  The check runs before `secrets.toml` is read, so a jj reachable only
  through its `jj_path` needs `TETHER_JJ`.
- **Run git code through a `git` object.** The `git` backend runs with
  `core.fsmonitor`, hooks and `ext::` transports off, and never takes a
  directory for a bare repository by itself (`safe.bareRepository`, which
  is why git 2.38 is required). A `git` object's `path` must be absolute and
  outside the checkout, whose files came with the clone.
- **Choose where writes go, or which pins `gc` releases.** Those are
  `workspace.toml` and the op log, refused when tracked. Another checkout's
  tracked copy is skipped with a warning naming the checkout.
- **Send your credentials somewhere.** Endpoints, and Icechunk's
  `allow_http` and `force_path_style`, come from `secrets.toml` only. A
  Dolt password goes only to a server `secrets.toml` lists.
- **Run SQL.** `[import] query` and `init_sql` come from `secrets.toml` or
  the command line. An import query runs as one statement in a read-only
  transaction.
- **Push your code.** A git object's `remote` must name a remote the
  repository already has.
- **Write outside `.tether/`.** Object keys are checked when a manifest is
  read, not only at `add`: no `..`, no `\`, no drive letters.

It can:

- **Name stores.** A locator is an address. A manifest can point `status`,
  `commit` and `verify` at any store your ambient credentials reach, and
  they sign the requests (a signature does not reveal the secret). `commit`
  records what it finds, a directory's file names and hashes included, and
  pushing publishes that.
- **Release pins in your stores, with your help.** `gc` releases only pins
  in its dataset's namespace that no manifest names and that this clone
  created. `--release-foreign` drops the last condition. In a clone that
  reuses another dataset's id and names its stores, that releases the other
  dataset's pins.
- **Make commands fail.** Every refusal above is an error: a hostile clone
  can stop a command, not redirect it.

So read a clone's manifests before its first `commit`, and a `gc` plan
before applying it. The dataset's own repository runs your git hooks on
dataset commits; those live in your `.git/`, which no clone brings.

## Workspace state

`.tether/workspace.toml` is per checkout (per jj workspace or git worktree):

```toml
workspace_id = "7c1e0a4d9b2e4f6a8c1d3e5f7a9b0c2d"
bookmark = "relabel"                 # the dataset bookmark this checkout works on (absent: read-only)
last_snapshot_at = "2026-09-04T22:10:03.118Z"

[working_refs]                       # branches that exist (on the trunk: the upstream branches)
"zarr/imaging" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"
"db/metrics" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"

[pending_forks]                      # decided by `new`, created on first writable open
"features" = "tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel"

[pending_resets."features"]          # the head `new` reviewed and agreed to reset on that open
version = 9                          #   (a branch that moved since is refused instead)

[base_states."zarr/imaging"]         # committed state this working ref corresponds to
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"     #   (differs from the manifest => stale)

[fork_points."zarr/imaging"]         # base state when the branch was forked (for promote)
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"

[last_snapshot."zarr/imaging"]       # what a plain `status` shows (errors are kept too)
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
```

A writable `open` moves an entry from `pending_forks` to `working_refs`.
`pending_resets` keeps it from resetting a branch that moved since `new`,
and `base_states` drive the stale check. Every `open` re-reads the file, so
a long-lived `Repo` follows what another process's `new` wrote.

## Operation log

`.tether/ops.jsonl` is this checkout's operation log: one JSON line per
store-writing command, appended only, like jj's `op log`. The VCS records
the manifests, but it cannot see which refs `commit` created, which
branches `new` forked or reset, what `gc` deleted, or where `promote` moved
a base branch from. Each entry holds the plan it applied, what it did, and
what it replaced. `tether ops` lists the entries, and `tether undo`
reverses from them.

The log is a journal. A store-writing command appends its entry and syncs
it *before* the first side effect, appends a progress record as each effect
lands, and marks completion with the result. A process killed in between
leaves an `INCOMPLETE` entry. `undo` refuses it, `repair --dry-run` says
how far it got, and running the command again finishes what is left. The
`new` and `gc` a `drop` runs are journaled as its steps (`parent`). An
interruption loses at most the line being written, and the next entry
starts on a fresh line.

Other commands read the log too, so deleting it loses more than `undo`:

- `gc` keeps every pin an unfinished operation in any live checkout set out
  to create;
- `status` and `ops` flag dataset commits that vanished from the VCS;
- the first `gc` seeds the [pin index](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#pins-this-clone-did-not-create)
  from the logs, so pins whose entries are gone by then are kept as
  another clone's.

## Environment variables

Every variable tether reads (`TETHER_REV`, `TETHER_JJ` / `TETHER_GIT`,
`TETHER_PUBLISH_DSN`, `NEON_API_KEY`, the Dolt `*_env` names, the cloud
credential chains) is in one table in the
[CLI Guide](07-cli.qmd#versions-and-environment), with the `GIT_*`
variables tether ignores.
